title: Matrix nanoalignment programs macrophage vesicular immunity through TRPV2 mechanogating

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Matrix nanoalignment programs macrophage vesicular immunity through TRPV2 mechanogating》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0035】The tumor microenvironment (TME) is shaped not only by its cellular heterogeneity but also by the dynamic and evolving architecture of the extracellular matrix (ECM), which undergoes extensive remodeling during tumor progression [[1], [2], [3]]. Progressive desmoplasia alters matrix density, fiber alignment, and topographical anisotropy, generating complex biophysical cues that regulate cancer cell behavior, immune infiltration, and therapeutic response [[4], [5], [6], [7], [8]]. Although the effects of ECM stiffness, viscoelasticity, and porosity on cancer biology have been intensively studied [[9], [10], [11]], less is known about how nanoscale architectural features, such as ligand orientation and fibrillar alignment, instruct immune-cell function [12,13]. These structural cues reorganize adhesion geometry and force transmission at the cell–matrix interface, thereby activating signaling programs that are distinct from those induced by bulk matrix mechanics [[14], [15], [16]].

【Introduction · p0040】ECM alignment is increasingly recognized as a physical hallmark of aggressive tumors [17]. Collagen fiber anisotropy correlates with invasion, metastasis, immune exclusion, and poor therapeutic response across multiple cancer types. In melanoma, dense and aligned ECM is a prominent feature of advanced disease and has been linked to poor responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade, increased macrophage infiltration, and immune suppression [18]. These observations suggest that ECM architecture, beyond matrix stiffness alone, may actively contribute to immune suppression in melanoma. However, because fibrotic tumor stroma contains intertwined biochemical, cellular, and mechanical changes, it remains difficult to determine whether nanoscale ECM alignment itself is sufficient to regulate behaviors of immune cells.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Matrix nanoalignment programs macrophage vesicular immunity through TRPV2 mechanogating》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · p0180】Our findings establish ECM nanoarchitecture as an active regulator of macrophage immune communication. By decoupling nanoscale ligand alignment from bulk matrix mechanics, the NAM/NIM platform demonstrates that adhesive nanoalignment is sufficient to enhance integrin β1-dependent mechanosensing and TRPV2-mediated Ca2+ signaling in TAMs. Downstream PI3K signaling bifurcates into a Rab11a-dependent branch that controls sEV trafficking and release and an mTORC2-associated branch that contributes to immunoregulatory cargo remodeling (Fig. 8). Together, these separable effects on vesicle output and particle-normalized cargo composition generate an sEV population preferentially enriched in anti-inflammatory cytokines, miR-181a-5p, and selected tissue-remodeling proteins, thereby suppressing TLR4–NF-κB signaling, reinforcing M2-like macrophage states, limiting CD8+ T-cell infiltration, and accelerating melanoma progression.

【Conclusion · p0185】These results advance the field in three respects. First, they identify nanoscale ECM alignment as a distinct physical cue capable of regulating macrophage secretory behavior independently of bulk stiffness. Second, they define separable Rab11a- and mTORC2-associated outputs downstream of a common mechanosensitive PI3K node, corresponding to sEV release and cargo remodeling, respectively. Third, they show that preferential intervention in the TRPV2–Rab11a pathway or TGF-β-associated matrix remodeling can reduce circulating sEV abundance, alleviate tumor immunosuppression, and restrict melanoma growth.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Matrix nanoalignment programs macrophage vesicular immunity through TRPV2 mechanogating》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 Characterization of the aligned ECM niche in melanoma and a magnetically switchable matrix nanoalignment system for regulating macrophage mechanosensing and sEV biogenesis. (a) Schematic illustration of aligned ECM architectures in melanoma that may enhance mechanosensing in attached tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and program their small extracellular vesicle (sEV) biogenesis and cargo. Parts of the figure were generated using BioRender.com. (b) TEM images showing aligned ECM structures in the intratumoral and peripheral regions of murine melanoma. Scale bars: 2 μm (left) and 200 nm (magnified view). (c) Schematic design of a magnetically switchable matrix that decouples nanoscale alignment from bulk matrix stiffness. The initial nonmagnetic state is a nanoscale isotropic matrix (NIM), whereas application of a lateral magnetic field induces a nanoscale aligned matrix (NAM). (d) HAADF-STEM images of nanofiber-mimetic nanorods (NMNs) with corresponding elemental mapping of Fe and Si (dashed outline). (e) SEM images of NIM and NAM. Scale bar: 200 nm. (f) Angular distributions of NMNs within NIM and NAM (n = 100 nanorods from three independent gels). (g) Stiffness measurements of NIM and NAM (n = 6). (h) Violin plots of average rupture forces measured on NIM and NAM (n = 40 from three independent gels). Data are presented as mean ± SD. Statistical significance was determined by unpaired t-test. ***p ≤ 0.001; ns, not significant.

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 Matrix nanoalignment enhances TAM mechanosensing and polarization more effectively than bulk matrix stiffness. (a) Calcein-AM/propidium iodide (PI) staining of macrophages cultured on NIM or NAM for 24 h, with or without immunoblockade of CD44 (anti-CD44) or integrin β1 (anti-β1). Scale bar: 200 μm. (b) Quantification of macrophage attachment (n = 4). (c) F-actin stress fiber staining of macrophages cultured on NIM or NAM with or without (w/o) cRGD coupling. Scale bar: 50 μm. (d) Rose plots showing peak orientation angles of macrophages cultured on NIM or NAM; the magnetic field direction was set at 90°. (e) Schematic comparison of the regulatory effects of NAM and cRGD-coupled matrices with stiffness ranging from soft to stiff on macrophage adhesion. (f) Corresponding stiffness measurements (n = 4). (g) Quantification of cell spreading and (h) shape factor after 24 h of incubation (n = 20 cells from three independent hydrogels). Scale bar: 50 μm. (i,j) Confocal images of iNOS and Arg-1 immunostaining with corresponding gene expression (n = 4) and cytokine secretion analysis (TNF-α and IL-10, n = 4) under pro-inflammatory (i) or anti-inflammatory (j) conditions. (k) Hierarchical clustering heatmap of M1-and M2-associated gene expression (row-normalized Z-scores; n = 3). Data are presented as mean ± SD. Statistical significance was determined by one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple-comparison test. *p ≤ 0.05, **p ≤ 0.01, ***p ≤ 0.001; ns, not significant.

【Fig. 3 · fig3】Fig. 3 Matrix nanoalignment enhances TAM-derived sEV secretion through activation of TRPV2/PI3K signaling. (a) Western blot analysis of whole-cell lysates (WCLs) and isolated sEVs from TAMs primed on NIM or NAM, with or without the TRPV2 inhibitor tranilast. (b) Representative nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) profiles of isolated sEVs. Insets show TEM images of collected sEVs from the corresponding groups. Scale bar: 100 nm. (c) Quantification of sEV secretion. sEV concentrations were normalized to the number of viable adherent donor cells and then expressed relative to the NIM group (set to 1; n = 3). (d) Representative TEM images showing vesicles released from the plasma membrane, indicated by white arrows. Ex: extracellular; Cy: cytoplasm. White dotted lines represent cell membrane boundary. Scale bar: 200 nm. (e) KEGG pathway enrichment and GO enrichment analyses of genes upregulated in the NAM group. Bubble size represents gene count; color indicates −log10(Q value). (f) Fluo-4 AM staining images with corresponding quantification of Ca2+ influx over time in the NIM and NAM groups with or without tranilast treatment. Scale bars: 20 μm. (g) Immunofluorescence images of Rab11a and CD63 showing their colocalization. Scale bars: 10 μm and 2 μm (magnified). (h) Quantitative analysis of measured colocalization between Rab11a and CD63 by Mander's overlap coefficient with Costes (≥95%), involving at least 10 cells from each of three independently prepared hydrogels. (i) Immunoblot analysis of total and phosphorylated PI3K, and total and GTP-bound Rab11a. (j) GSEA plots showing enrichment of hallmark pathways in NAM-cultured macrophages, including the Rho GTPase cycle and vesicle tethering complex. Data are presented as mean ± SD. Statistical significance was determined by one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple-comparison test. **p ≤ 0.01; ***p ≤ 0.001.
